theme: 3 terms on error handling follow-ups: making a type throwable, returning success or failure, and throwing only when a closure throws

terms.definition: A protocol that a type adopts so its values can be thrown as errors.
terms.example: Our `LoginError` enum conforms to the Error protocol, so we can throw its cases.

terms.definition: A type that holds either a success value or a failure error, so a function can return it instead of throwing.
terms.example: The completion handler passes a Result type, so the caller switches on `.success` and `.failure`.

terms.definition: A keyword that marks a function that throws only when the closure passed to it throws.
terms.example: Mark the helper as rethrows, so callers with safe closures don't need `try`.

quizzes.question: What do you call a type that holds either a success value or a failure error?
What do you call a function that can only fail when the closure you pass to it fails?
What must your custom enum adopt before you can throw its cases?

Learn to talk about Swift errors without throwing everywhere: Error Protocol, Result Type & Rethrows, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Error Protocol - A protocol that a type adopts so its values can be thrown as errors.
Result Type - A type that holds either a success value or a failure error, so a function can return it instead of throwing.
Rethrows - A keyword that marks a function that throws only when the closure passed to it throws.

Explain Error Protocol, Result Type & Rethrows in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
에러 프로토콜, Result 타입, rethrows 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Error Protocol - A protocol that a type adopts so its values can be thrown as errors.
한국어: 에러 프로토콜: 타입이 채택하면 그 값을 에러로 던질 수 있게 해 주는 프로토콜

Result Type - A type that holds either a success value or a failure error, so a function can return it instead of throwing.
한국어: Result 타입: 성공 값 또는 실패 에러 중 하나를 담아, 던지는 대신 반환할 수 있게 하는 타입

Rethrows - A keyword that marks a function that throws only when the closure passed to it throws.
한국어: rethrows: 전달받은 클로저가 에러를 던질 때만 함수도 에러를 던진다고 표시하는 키워드

dialogue.title: Errors you can return

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, I can't throw `offline`. The compiler says `LoadError` doesn't conform to Error.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your enum needs the Error Protocol. Add it after `LoadError`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, I forgot. So any type with the Error Protocol can be thrown?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Now look at `load`. It doesn't throw at all.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yeah, it returns a Result Type with `success` or `failure`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. A Result Type is handy when you pass the outcome to a completion handler.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then why does `retry` need `try` inside? I thought it never throws.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It can. It's marked Rethrows, so it throws only if `f` throws.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the `print` line with `cached` needs no `try`?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Correct. With Rethrows, a closure that can't fail means no `try` at the call site.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. I'll use that for the cache helper too.
Want to throw your enum? Make it conform to the Error protocol.
